study type: secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized trial
exposure: timing of maternal discharge (postoperative day 2, 3, or >=4)
cohort: The study included 1,391 women who underwent unscheduled cesarean delivery, excluding those with hypertensive disorders or infections diagnosed prior to postoperative day 2.
finding: The risk of the maternal postpartum composite outcome (readmission, unscheduled clinic, or ER visit) was significantly higher in patients discharged on postoperative day 3 or >=4 compared to those discharged on postoperative day 2 following unscheduled cesarean delivery.
